target.notes: Mounted with default configuration, following the Radix documentation. No focus management, ARIA attributes or key handlers added by the adapter.

assertions.title: The combobox has an accessible name
assertions.rationale: Without a name, a screen reader announces an unlabelled combobox and the user has no idea what they are choosing.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: The input exposes role=combobox
assertions.rationale: The role is what tells assistive technology that this input has a popup, and enables the announcements and shortcuts that go with it.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: The combobox can be reached with the Tab key
assertions.rationale: If Tab does not reach it, a keyboard user cannot use the control at all.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: aria-expanded is present and false before the popup opens
assertions.rationale: aria-expanded is how a screen reader announces that this control has a popup and that it is currently shut. Omitting it until opening leaves the user unaware there is anything to open.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: Down Arrow opens the popup
assertions.rationale: Down Arrow is the APG-specified way to open the list. If it does nothing, a keyboard user has no way to browse the options.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: aria-expanded becomes true when the popup opens
assertions.rationale: A sighted user sees the list appear. Without the state change, a screen reader user is never told it did.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: The popup exposes role=listbox
assertions.rationale: The listbox role is what makes the popup navigable as a set of options rather than announced as unstructured content.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: The combobox references its popup with aria-controls
assertions.rationale: The relationship is what lets assistive technology connect the input to the list it drives, rather than treating them as unrelated regions.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: Each option exposes role=option
assertions.rationale: Without the option role, a screen reader cannot count the choices, announce position within them, or let the user jump between them.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: Down Arrow moves through the options
assertions.rationale: Browsing the list is the entire purpose of the control. If the arrow keys do not move between options, a keyboard user cannot reach anything but the first.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: The active option is exposed to assistive technology
assertions.rationale: A sighted user sees the highlight move. Unless it is communicated through aria-activedescendant or DOM focus, a screen reader user is never told which option they are on.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: DOM focus stays on the combobox while the popup is open
assertions.rationale: The APG pattern keeps focus on the input so the user can keep typing to filter while browsing. Moving focus into the list breaks that and is a common source of confusing behaviour.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: Enter selects the active option
assertions.rationale: Selecting is the point of the control. If Enter does not commit the active option, a keyboard user can browse the list but never choose from it.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.

assertions.title: Escape closes the popup
assertions.rationale: Escape is the learned way out. Without it a user who opened the list by accident has no obvious way to dismiss it.
assertions.reason: Radix UI does not ship a combobox primitive. Its Select implements the APG select-only pattern, which has different requirements and is scored separately.
